messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2: model artifact fetch failures from huggingface.co observed in prod. 18% of model pull attempts returning 429/503 over the last 7m. Paging oncall. thread: 1919876543

maya (SRE): got it, oncall pinged. i'm checking ingestion/errors dashboard now — latency spike and errors line up with HF 429s.

oncall (night): i'm up, looking. which model(s) impacted?

alex (runtime): looks like it's mainly large BLOOM/opt quantized artifacts we fetch during cold starts. sample error from runtime: ```2026-03-15T02:12:03Z ERROR model_fetcher_fetch: GET https://huggingface.co/some-org/large-model/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin -> 429 Too Many Requests (x-retry=3)```

kevin (platform): HF status page shows degraded artifact CDN earlier: https://status.huggingface.co/ incidents note: "rate limiting for heavy artifact consumption". they've posted mitigation but still throttling.

jen (support): we've got 3 active customer tickets reporting timeouts on generation endpoints — users seeing 504s and elevated latencies since ~01:55 UTC. Customer-impact batch: sandbox customers + a small number of prod tenants with low replication.

maya (SRE): impact assessment: ~2-4% of requests are failing fast (no model loaded), + a tail latency increase for cold-starts up to +12s. warm instances unaffected.

alex (runtime): current runtime behavior: on model-missing we try to pull from HF, with up to 3 immediate retries and exponential backoff. cache miss -> start download -> block request. we should enable async fetch + proxy fallback ASAP.

mike (eng): options I'd recommend now: 1) enable fallback to smaller model variant (already packaged locally), 2) reduce concurrent pulls per host (limit to 1), 3) turn on aggressive backoff and request queueing for model pulls, 4) if possible, switch model registry to our S3 mirror for affected artifacts.

kevin (platform): implementing (2) & (3) now: lowering max_concurrent_model_downloads to 1 and increasing backoff base to 5s. patch rolling to model-fetchers in staging, then prod. will push in ~3m.

alex (runtime): patch applied to one canary host, verified fail/retry code paths. can run a controlled canary: if HF returns 429, we fallback to pre-bundled small-quant model and mark the request as degraded but served.

jen (support): please post an interim public status note so customers know we're mitigating and there may be degraded responses. I'll draft a blurb.

jenaction (support): DRAFT: "We are investigating increased model fetch failures caused by a third-party artifact host. Some requests may return degraded responses or timeouts. Engineers are applying fallbacks and reducing concurrent downloads to mitigate. We'll update in 30m." add link to status page. :thumbsup:

hf-status-bot: huggingface incident update: "Artifact CDN throttling remains active; we're coordinating with customers to prioritize heavy consumers." (automated)

maya (SRE): mitigation log so far: - reduced concurrent downloads cluster-wide (partial rollout) - enabled aggressive backoff - canary configured to fallback to local small model - created mirror job to sync hot artifacts to our S3 mirror (manual trigger).

ops-lead: how long until mirror is warmed?

kevin (platform): mirror job started at 02:25 UTC copying prioritized model shards (list: large-model v1, opt-13b-quant, llm-lite). estimate 12-18m for initial hotset. once mirrored, we'll change registry mapping for pulls to point to S3 for these models.

mike (eng): temp workaround for very high-importance customers: we can pin them to dedicated pre-warmed instances (they'll still pay) — suggest offering that while HF is degraded.

oncall (night): i'm switching incident owner to maya for the next 40m (need to sleep) — maya, taking handover.

maya (SRE): taking it. summary: HF artifact CDN rate limits causing model pulls to fail -> increased cold-start latencies and a small number of 504s. active mitigations: concurrent downloads limited, backoff increased, local fallback to smaller model enabled on canary, mirror job running, customer comms posted.

jen (support): posted customer status update and linked to this thread. inbound tickets decreased after early notices.

alex (runtime): observed canary behavior: when HF returns 429 we now do: async queue + try local fallback. sample log: ```INFO serve_request: model=large-model action=fallback_to_small variant=quant-small reason=hf_429``` requests served but with lower throughput.

maya (SRE): measurement: after partial rollout p95 cold-start went from +12s -> +4s on canary hosts. errors from pull attempts down from 18% -> 6% (since backoff & queueing).

hf-status-bot: update: "We are enabling temporary rate limit boosts for verified customers; contact support@huggingface.co with request id."

kevin (platform): mirror sync completed for high-priority artifacts at 02:39 UTC. switching registry mapping for affected models to S3 now (hot swap).

alex (runtime): registry mapping switched on canary, verified downloads served from S3 mirror with normal latency. will roll to prod after 3m of stability.

maya (SRE): prod roll started, expected finish in 6m. continuing to monitor errors and customer tickets.

ops-lead: please keep incident timeline and actions for postmortem. assign owner for follow-up: kevin and alex for infra/runtime changes, jen for customer comms.

jen (support): assigned. I'll follow up with impacted customers with details and remediation timeline.

mike (eng): recommend adding a scheduled prefetch/warm pool for large models to avoid future cold-start exposure to external registries. logging action item.

maya (SRE): agreed. logged follow-ups: PREFETCH-42 (prefetch warm pool), MIRROR-17 (mirror automation + ACL), RUNTIME-98 (async fetch + graceful degrade default).

oncall (night): back briefly — thanks team, handing back to maya in 20m for continuity. i'll still be reachable for pager escalations.

maya (SRE): rolling update complete at 02:51 UTC. post-mitigation stats: pull errors ~1.2%, cold-start tail reduced. customers on pinned pre-warmed instances unaffected.

jen (support): outbound customer notes updated with mirror info and temporary mitigation steps. close-loop with accounts team.

maya (SRE): incident severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 02:55 UTC — continuing monitoring and follow-ups. will start postmortem doc after stab. handoff: oncall->maya remains owner until morning shift.

ops-lead: nice work. timeline/events and logs captured. we'll schedule a postmortem and coordinate with HF for SLA/priority handling.

(incident thread closed for now; further updates will be appended here)
